summary:
Huánuco stands under Peru's national framework: Peru does not criminalise trans identity, but the national Congress has legislated against trans people's use of public facilities, hate-crime protection for LGBT people has been removed from the Penal Code, and recorded violence against trans women is rising.

On 2 April 2025 the plenary of Congress approved and waived a second vote on the dictamen of the Ley que fortalece el derecho a la indemnidad sexual de los niños y adolescentes. Its Article 5.1 prohibits any person from entering or using a public sanitary facility designated for a sex other than their birth sex, with narrow exceptions for custody and for cases where required, such as accompanying minors, elderly people or people with disabilities; venues are also barred from posting ambiguous restroom signs. The Comisión de Mujer y Familia had approved the merged dictamen of bills 6506 and 8457, sponsored by Jorge Montoya and Alejandro Muñante, unanimously on 20 February 2025. The trigger was a July 2023 complaint over gendered restroom labels at Lima's Jorge Chávez international airport.

Enforcement of the restroom restriction would rest on security staff checking the DNI to decide whether a woman entering a women's restroom is trans or cisgender, according to activist Gianna Camacho. The IDEHPUCP human-rights institute reads Article 5 as a direct breach of Article 2(2) of the Peruvian Constitution and Article 1.1 of the American Convention on Human Rights, resting on the stereotype that trans people are more prone to enter restrooms to harass or sexually abuse minors. Documented cases of trans people barred from public restrooms include SPC-INDECOPI Resolution 0735-2022, which dismissed a trans woman's discrimination complaint against SmartFit after the company grounded bathroom assignment on the sex recorded in her DNI; gender-identity recognition in Peru remains long, costly and invasive.

Recorded violence against trans people is rising and undercounts the reality. Peru recorded 54 killings of TLGBI people and 170 rights-violation cases between 2020 and 2023, according to the Observatorio de Derechos TLGBI of Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia; the homicide victims were 30 trans women, 23 gay men and one lesbian. Nineteen killings occurred in 2023 alone, 12 of them trans women, and killers were not identified in 26 of the 54 homicides, including 13 of 19 in 2023. These are raw national counts without a per-capita denominator, so they rank volume of cases rather than comparative risk between jurisdictions.

The February 2023 murder of trans sex worker Rubi Torres Silvano (31), kidnapped from central Lima by a 'Los Gallegos' extortion gang and killed in Carabayllo with some 30 gunshots, followed the shooting of Priscila Aguado Huatuco (30) days earlier; two killers were arrested in March 2023. The state has not incorporated sexual orientation or gender identity into its crime-registration systems, so hate crimes cannot be prosecuted as such.
tangentialFactors:
The restroom restriction's practical reach depends on venue security and DNI checks, a mechanism that would apply equally in Huánuco's shopping centres, gyms and transport hubs as in Lima. The SmartFit precedent shows a private operator can lawfully assign facilities by DNI-recorded sex and have a discrimination complaint dismissed, so trans visitors in Huánuco should expect venue staff to follow the document rather than presentation.

Huánuco's own contribution to the national violence tally is not separately identified in the sources; the 54 killings and 170 violation cases are national aggregates covering 2020–2023 and are reported as raw counts without population adjustment. The absence of sexual orientation and gender identity fields in state crime-registration systems means no jurisdiction-level breakdown of hate crime by department exists to compare Huánuco against other regions.
localsOnly:
Residents of Huánuco live under the same national facility restriction as the rest of Peru: entry to public restrooms is tied to birth sex as recorded, with security staff potentially checking DNI. Gender-identity recognition remains a long, costly and invasive judicial process, and the 2022 INDECOPI resolution shows administrative complaints on restroom access have been dismissed.

Trans women in Peru face documented elevated exposure to lethal violence, with 30 of 54 recorded LGBTI homicide victims between 2020 and 2023 being trans women, and killers unidentified in nearly half of cases. Because the state does not record sexual orientation or gender identity in crime systems, residents cannot report an incident as a hate crime and have it registered as such.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Huánuco-specific incident, enforcement action, local ordinance or institution appears in the source inventory; all findings are national-layer and carried by the parent record. Whether Huánuco venues have applied DNI-based restroom checks, or whether any local complaint has been filed, is not sourced and remains unresolved.

The sources do not state whether the April 2025 sexual-integrity law's Article 5.1 has been enforced in practice anywhere, including Huánuco, nor whether any constitutional challenge to it has been filed or decided. The status of the pending Gender Identity Law as of any date after March 2021 is also not sourced here.
